s: In which year was the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) launched?
x: The BRI was launched in 2013.

s: In which country is Kyaukphyu port located?
x: Kyaukphyu is in Myanmar; Hambantota is in Sri Lanka, Gwadar in Pakistan and Chittagong in Bangladesh.

s: Why does India mainly oppose the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor?
o: excludes Pakistan from the Belt and Road Initiative
was established under the Panchsheel Agreement
passes through PoJK, raising a sovereignty issue
connects only Indian ports with Chinese ports
x: India's objection is that CPEC passes through Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, creating a sovereignty concern.

s: Where was the India-China anti-terror army exercise 'Hand-in-Hand' first held in 2007?
x: Hand-in-Hand, the India-China anti-terror army exercise, was first held in 2007 at Kunming.

s: Which of the following China-Pakistan exercise-service pairs is correctly matched?
x: Shaheen is the air force exercise; Warrior is the army and Sea Guardian the navy exercise.

s: Which of the following port-country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Chittagong is in Bangladesh, not Myanmar; the other pairs are correct.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Johnson Line – Places Aksai Chin in Ladakh
McMahon Line – Places Aksai Chin under China
Macartney-MacDonald Line – Places Aksai Chin in Ladakh
Johnson Line – Eastern boundary between Tibet and India
x: The Johnson Line places Aksai Chin in Ladakh. The Macartney-MacDonald Line places it under China, and the McMahon Line is the eastern Tibet-India boundary.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Macartney-MacDonald Line — 1865, places Aksai Chin in Ladakh
McMahon Line — Western boundary in Ladakh
x: The McMahon Line was drawn at the Simla Convention of 1914 by Henry McMahon as the eastern Tibet-India boundary. The Johnson Line dates from 1865 (W.H. Johnson) and places Aksai Chin in Ladakh, which is India's claim. The Macartney-MacDonald Line (1899) places Aksai Chin under China. The McMahon Line is in the eastern sector, not Ladakh.

s: China occupies about how much Indian territory in Aksai Chin?
x: China occupies about 38,000 sq km in Aksai Chin; the ~90,000 sq km figure is its claim in the north-east (most of Arunachal Pradesh).

s: The Shaksgam Valley, also known as the Trans-Karakoram Tract, was ceded to China by Pakistan under which agreement?
o: 1993 India-China Agreement on Peace and Tranquillity
x: Pakistan illegally ceded the Shaksgam Valley to China under the 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement. India regards it as an integral part of India.

s: On which date did India recognise the People's Republic of China?
x: India recognised the PRC on 30 December 1949 and established diplomatic ties on 1 April 1950, as the first non-socialist-bloc country to do so.

s:
Consider the following statements about Arunachal Pradesh in India-China relations:
1. China claims about 90,000 sq km in the north-east, most of it in Arunachal.
2. China denied visas to Arunachal members of India's delegation in 1995.
3. The USA has reaffirmed Arunachal as part of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: China claims ~90,000 sq km ('South Tibet'), denied visas in 1995 (Beijing women's conference), and the USA reaffirmed Arunachal as Indian.

s: Which boundary line represents India's claim over Aksai Chin?
x: The Johnson Line (1865) put Aksai Chin in Ladakh, India's claim; the Macartney-MacDonald Line placed it under China.

s: By what name does China refer to Arunachal Pradesh in its territorial claim?
x: China claims about 90,000 sq km in the north-east, most of Arunachal Pradesh, which it calls 'South Tibet'.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the sectors of the Line of Actual Control?
o: The Western sector comprises Ladakh and includes Aksai Chin
The Middle sector is the most contested sector
The Middle sector comprises Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
The Eastern sector comprises Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh and is associated with the McMahon Line
x: The Middle sector is the least contested sector of the LAC.

s: What is the approximate length of the India-China border?
x: The India-China border is approximately 3,488 km long.

s: Which States does the Middle sector of the LAC, the least contested, cover?
x: The Middle sector covers Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand; Ladakh is the Western and Sikkim-Arunachal the Eastern sector.

s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a cause of the India-China war of 1962?
o: The Tibet question and the Dalai Lama's asylum in 1959
The unsettled boundary left without a clear line by the British
x: The 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement followed the 1962 war and was not a cause of it. The unsettled boundary, the Tibet question and India's Forward Policy were identified causes.

s: How did the India-China war of 1962 (20 October-21 November) end?
x: The war ended in China's unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962, not a negotiated one.

s: Which report (1963) reviewed India's military failure in the 1962 war with China?
x: The Henderson Brooks-Bhagat Report (1963) reviewed India's military failure in 1962.

s: The 1962 India-China war was fought in which two sectors?
x: The war was fought in Aksai Chin (west) and NEFA (east).

s: In which year was the Dalai Lama granted asylum in India, a cause of the 1962 war?
x: The Dalai Lama got asylum in India in 1959, one of the causes of the 1962 war.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding recent India–China relations?
o: The Special Representatives mechanism dates from 2003
The 25th round of Special Representatives' talks was held in Beijing in August 2026
Ten PLA brigades were reported to remain on the LAC
India holds that relations can become normal even if the border remains unsettled and tense
x: India's stated position is that relations cannot be normal until the border is peaceful.

s: Which agreement was signed in 1993 during Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao's visit to China?
o: Agreement on Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC
Agreement on Confidence-Building Measures in the Military Field
Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the Boundary Question
x: The 1993 Agreement on Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC was associated with Prime Minister Narasimha Rao's visit.

s: What did the 2005 agreement between India and China deal with?
o: Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for settlement of the boundary question
Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC
x: The 2005 agreement laid down Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for settlement of the boundary question.

s: Over which region did India accept China's sovereignty under the 1954 Panchsheel Agreement?
x: India accepted China's sovereignty over Tibet under the 1954 Panchsheel Agreement.

s: In which year was the India-China Border Defence Cooperation Agreement signed?
x: The BDCA was signed in 2013; 2005 was the Political Parameters agreement, 2012 the WMCC and 2003 the Special Representatives.

s: Where was the 25th round of India-China Special Representatives' talks (August 2026), which issued an eight-point document on the LAC, held?
x: The 25th round was held in Beijing; the 24th round (August 2025) was held in New Delhi.

s: Under which Prime Minister was the Special Representatives mechanism for India-China boundary talks set up in 2003?
x: The SR mechanism dates to 2003 (Vajpayee); the 1993 Peace and Tranquillity agreement was under Narasimha Rao.

s: What does the India-China Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC), set up in 2012, deal with?
x: The WMCC (2012) handles border affairs, not settlement; settlement talks are with the Special Representatives (2003).

s: In which year did India and China sign the Agreement on Confidence-Building Measures in the Military Field?
x: The CBMs in the Military Field agreement was signed in 1996, after the 1993 Peace and Tranquillity agreement.

s: In which year did the India-China standoff at Doklam take place?
x: Sumdorong Chu was in 1986-87, Depsang 2013, Doklam 2017 and Galwan 2020.

s: Where did the Doklam standoff of 2017 occur?
x: The Doklam standoff occurred at the India-Bhutan-China tri-junction.

s: Where was the Modi-Xi meeting held that endorsed the October 2024 understanding on Depsang and Demchok?
x: The understanding was endorsed at the Modi-Xi meeting in Kazan in October 2024.

s: How many Indian soldiers were killed in the Galwan Valley clash in Eastern Ladakh on 15 June 2020?
x: Twenty Indian soldiers were killed in the Galwan clash of 15 June 2020 in Eastern Ladakh.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about disengagement at LAC friction points?
o: Gogra-Hot Springs disengagement took place in 2020
Pangong Tso north and south banks disengagement took place in 2021
Depsang and Demchok came under the October 2024 understanding
Galwan was among the disengagement points
x: Gogra-Hot Springs disengagement took place in 2022, not 2020; the other statements are correct.

s: Which of the following standoff-place pairs is correctly matched?
x: Sumdorong Chu (1986-87) was in Tawang; Depsang was in Ladakh, Yangtse in Tawang and Doklam at the India-Bhutan-China tri-junction.

s: On which date did the Yangtse clash in Tawang between Indian and Chinese troops take place?
x: The Yangtse clash in Tawang was on 9 December 2022; 15 June 2020 was Galwan.

s: Where is the Mudh-Nyoma airbase, built by the BRO at about 13,000 ft, located?
x: Mudh-Nyoma is in eastern Ladakh, facing the western sector of the LAC.

s: In which year did the Depsang standoff between India and China take place?
x: The Depsang standoff in Ladakh took place in 2013; Doklam was 2017 and Galwan 2020.

s: When did the India-China standoff at Sumdorong Chu in Tawang take place?
x: The Sumdorong Chu standoff in Tawang took place in 1986-87.

s: The mobile application bans imposed in 2020 in the context of India-China relations were made under which provision?
o: Section 79A of the Information Technology Act
Section 69A of the Information Technology Act
Section 66A of the Information Technology Act
Section 72A of the Information Technology Act
x: The 2020 application bans were imposed under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act.

s: In which year was the India-China Strategic Economic Dialogue set up?
x: The SED was set up in 2010 and held six rounds (2011-2019); 2013 is the BRI launch year.

s: FDI from which countries requires government approval under Press Note 3 of 2020?
o: Countries sharing a land border with India
Countries without a tax treaty with India
x: Press Note 3 requires government approval for FDI from countries sharing a land border with India; it does not ban such investment.

s: What is India's approximate trade deficit with China (July 2026)?
x: The trade deficit with China is about $100 billion, with dependence on machinery, APIs, electronics and solar.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India-China economic ties?
o: The 2020 app bans were made under Section 69A of the IT Act
The Strategic Economic Dialogue was set up in 2010
Press Note 3 (2020) bans FDI from land-border countries
India depends on China for APIs and solar equipment
x: Press Note 3 requires government approval for FDI from land-border countries; it is not a ban.

s: The mega dam being constructed by China on the upper course of the Brahmaputra is associated with which name of the river?
x: The Brahmaputra is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, where China is building the mega dam.

s: Besides the Brahmaputra, for which river do India and China have flood-season hydrological data MoUs?
x: The flood-season data MoUs cover the Brahmaputra and Sutlej; the Expert Level Mechanism deals with trans-border rivers.

s: Where is the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, of which India is a founding member, headquartered?
x: The AIIB is headquartered in Beijing, not New Delhi, and India is a founding member.

s: In which year was Nathu La in Sikkim reopened for border trade?
x: Nathu La reopened for trade in 2006; the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra resumed via Lipulekh and Nathu La.

s: In which year did India and China set up the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers?
x: The Expert Level Mechanism dates to 2006; flood-season data MoUs cover the Brahmaputra and Sutlej.

s: Where was the 18th BRICS Summit (September 2026) held?
x: The 18th BRICS Summit was held in New Delhi in September 2026.

s: Through which passes is the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra conducted?
x: The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra runs via Lipulekh (Uttarakhand) and Nathu La (Sikkim).

s: In which area did the 2007 revision of the India-Bhutan Friendship Treaty remove the provision that Bhutan would be guided by India?
x: The 2007 revision removed the clause that Bhutan would be guided by India in foreign affairs.

s: In which year was India's Friendship Treaty with Bhutan originally signed?
x: The India-Bhutan Friendship Treaty dates to 1949 (revised 2007); the Nepal treaty is of 1950.

s: Who led Myanmar's military coup of 1 February 2021?
x: The coup of 1 February 2021 brought the junta of Senior General Min Aung Hlaing to power; India engages it for Act East and north-east security.

s: With which Indian payment system was the Maldives' Favara system linked in August 2026?
x: Favara was linked with India's UPI in August 2026 as ties were repaired after 'India Out'.

s: The Kaladan Multimodal project connects which of the following routes?
o: Kolkata–Sittwe port–Kaladan river and road route to Mizoram
x: The Kaladan Multimodal project links Kolkata with Sittwe port and then uses the Kaladan river-road route to Mizoram.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's connectivity projects with neighbours?
o: Greater Male Connectivity is an undersea tunnel linking Male with Sri Lanka
The Akhaura-Agartala rail link connects Tripura through Bangladesh
The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway connects Moreh (Manipur) with Mae Sot
Broad-gauge cross-border rail lines with Nepal are under construction
x: Greater Male Connectivity is a bridge-causeway linking Male to nearby Maldivian islands, not a tunnel to Sri Lanka.

s: Where in India does the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway begin?
x: The Trilateral Highway runs from Moreh in Manipur to Mae Sot in Thailand.

s: Which Indian agency built the 218 km Zaranj-Delaram highway in Afghanistan?
x: The Zaranj-Delaram highway (218 km) was built by the BRO and links to the Iran border (Chabahar route).

s: What kind of project is the Greater Male Connectivity project in the Maldives?
x: Greater Male Connectivity is a bridge-causeway linking Male to nearby islands, not a tunnel.

s: On which river is Salma Dam, also known as the Afghan-India Friendship Dam, located?
x: Salma Dam is the Afghan-India Friendship Dam in Herat, constructed on the Hari Rud and inaugurated in 2016.

s: From which of the following projects does India import hydropower from Bhutan?
x: Mangdechhu (720 MW) is in Bhutan; India imports power from Bhutan. Arun III is in Nepal, Rooppur in Bangladesh, Salma in Afghanistan.

s: In which country is the Punatsangchhu hydroelectric project located?
x: Punatsangchhu I and II are India-backed hydro projects in Bhutan.

s: What is the capacity of the India-assisted Mangdechhu hydroelectric project in Bhutan?
x: Mangdechhu in Bhutan is a 720 MW project, inaugurated by the PM in 2019.

s: Which of the following was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Kabul in 2015?
x: The Afghan Parliament building in Kabul was inaugurated by Prime Minister Modi in 2015.

s: Which Indian Prime Minister visited Kabul in September 1959?
x: PM Nehru visited Kabul in September 1959.

s: In which year did India station a technical team in Kabul after the Taliban takeover of August 2021?
x: India sent a technical team to Kabul in 2022, besides wheat, medicine and vaccine aid.

s: With which organisation did India restore the Stor Palace in Kabul, completed in 2016?
x: The Stor Palace in Kabul was restored by India with the Aga Khan Trust for Culture and completed in 2016.

s: With which country is the 'India Out' campaign associated?
x: India Out is a Maldives issue; Teesta concerns Bangladesh, Rohingya Myanmar/Bangladesh and Doklam Bhutan.

s: Which of the following issue-country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Doklam tri-junction concerns Bhutan, not Nepal; the other pairs are correct.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Buddhist International Tourism Circuit promoted in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It targets pilgrims from Sri Lanka, Myanmar and Thailand.
It targets pilgrims from Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka only.
It targets pilgrims from Nepal, Bhutan and Afghanistan only.
It targets pilgrims from Bangladesh, China and Pakistan only.
x: The Buddhist International Tourism Circuit in Andhra Pradesh targets pilgrims from Sri Lanka, Myanmar and Thailand.

s: What happened under Operation Pawan?
o: IPKF was deployed in Sri Lanka
x: Operation Pawan was the Indian Peace Keeping Force operation in Sri Lanka, during which the IPKF eventually fought the LTTE.

s: India launched which operation to provide assistance after the Nepal earthquake of 2015?
x: Operation Maitri was launched by India in response to the Nepal earthquake of 2015.

s: Operation Cactus, launched by India in 1988, was associated with the foiling of a coup in which country?
x: Operation Cactus was the Indian operation that foiled a coup attempt in the Maldives in 1988.

s: Under the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement, implemented in 2015, how many Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh?
x: 111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves came to India.

s: For access to which enclaves was the Tin Bigha corridor leased to Bangladesh in 1992?
x: Tin Bigha was leased in 1992 to give Bangladesh access to the Dahagram-Angarpota enclaves.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act implemented the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement in 2015?
x: The 1974 Land Boundary Agreement was implemented in 2015 by the 100th Amendment.

s: In which year was the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement originally signed?
x: The Land Boundary Agreement was signed in 1974 and implemented in 2015 by the 100th Amendment.

s: The Ganga Water Treaty of 1996 is associated with which of the following features?
x: The 1996 Ganga Water Treaty with Bangladesh concerns Farakka and has a 30-year duration. It emerged in the context of the Gujral Doctrine's principle of non-reciprocity.

s: Who headed the elected government sworn in Bangladesh in February 2026?
x: After the 2024 upheaval, an elected government under Tarique Rahman was sworn in Bangladesh in February 2026.

s: What is the India-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline mainly?
x: The India-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline is a diesel pipeline connecting the two countries.

s: Which of the following project–country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Russia-built Rooppur nuclear plant is in Bangladesh, not Sri Lanka. Arun III is in Nepal, Mangdechhu in Bhutan and Maitree (Rampal) in Bangladesh.

s:
Consider the following statements about India-backed power projects in Bangladesh:
1. Rooppur is a nuclear power project built by Russia.
2. Maitree at Rampal is a hydroelectric project.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Maitree at Rampal is a thermal power project.

s: With which country is the Rohingya refugee issue chiefly linked?
x: The Rohingya issue concerns Myanmar (and Bangladesh, where many have fled).

s: With which of the following neighbours does India share its shortest land border (about 106 km)?
x: India's border with Afghanistan is only about 106 km, far shorter than with Bhutan (699 km), Myanmar (1,643 km) or Nepal (1,751 km).

s: Among the following, which country shares the longest border with India?
x: Bangladesh shares 4,096.7 km with India, China 3,488 km, Nepal 1,751 km and Bhutan 699 km.

s: With which neighbour does India share its second-longest land border?
x: Bangladesh (4,096.7 km) is first and China (3,488 km) second, ahead of Pakistan (3,323 km).

s: The Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 provided for provincial councils through which amendment of Sri Lanka's Constitution?
x: The 1987 Accord provided for provincial councils through the 13th Amendment, along with the merger of the Northern and Eastern provinces and the IPKF.

s: The Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 provided for the merger of which provinces of Sri Lanka?
x: The 1987 Accord (Rajiv Gandhi-Jayewardene) provided for merging the Northern and Eastern provinces and devolution under the 13th Amendment.

s: In which year did Sri Lanka crush the LTTE?
x: Sri Lanka crushed the LTTE in 2009; it had killed Rajiv Gandhi in 1991 and India banned it in 1992.

s: Who signed the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 with Rajiv Gandhi?
x: The 1987 Accord was signed by Rajiv Gandhi and J.R. Jayewardene.

s: On the order of which Prime Minister was the IPKF withdrawn from Sri Lanka (last troops left 24 March 1990)?
x: The IPKF was withdrawn on V.P. Singh's order; the last troops left on 24 March 1990.

s: In which year did India ban the LTTE?
x: India banned the LTTE in 1992 after it killed Rajiv Gandhi in 1991; the ban was not part of the 1987 Accord.

s: Which LTTE chief was killed when the Sri Lankan Army crushed the LTTE in 2009?
x: In 2009 the Sri Lankan Army defeated the LTTE and its chief V. Prabhakaran was killed.

s: In which country is the India-funded Kankesanthurai (KKS) port upgrade located?
x: Kankesanthurai port is near Jaffna in Sri Lanka.

s: Hambantota port in Sri Lanka is seen as part of India's encirclement by which country?
x: Hambantota is part of the Chinese, not Pakistani, encirclement (APPSC G1 2024).

s: Which country received India's economic crisis support of about $4 billion in 2022?
x: India gave Sri Lanka about $4 billion during its 2022 economic crisis.

s: Which treaty is associated with an open border and security cooperation, while Nepal seeks its revision?
o: India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950
x: The 1950 India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship provides for an open border and security cooperation; Nepal has sought its revision.

s: The Kalapani-Limpiyadhura-Lipulekh dispute is linked with which historical treaty and later development?
o: Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 and Sri Lanka's map of 2015
Gujral Doctrine of 1996 and Bhutan's map of 2007
Sugauli Treaty of 1816 and Nepal's new map of 2020
Treaty of Peace and Friendship of 1950 and Bangladesh's map of 1974
x: The dispute is linked to the Sugauli Treaty of 1816 and Nepal's new map issued in 2020.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Mahakali Treaty was concluded with Nepal, not Bangladesh, in 1996. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's water agreements with Nepal:
1. The Kosi Agreement was signed in 1954.
2. The Gandak Agreement was signed in 1996.
3. The Mahakali Treaty covers Sarada, Tanakpur and Pancheshwar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Gandak Agreement was signed in 1959, not 1996.

s: With which country did India sign the Mahakali Treaty of 1996?
x: The Mahakali Treaty (Sarada, Tanakpur, Pancheshwar) is with Nepal; the 1996 Ganga Water Treaty is with Bangladesh.

s: Who was the first President of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal?
x: Ram Baran Yadav was the first President; Prachanda was the first Prime Minister.

s: When was Nepal's new Constitution adopted?
x: Nepal adopted its new Constitution on 20 September 2015; the monarchy was abolished on 28 May 2008.

s: When did Nepal's first Constituent Assembly abolish the monarchy?
x: Nepal's first Constituent Assembly abolished the monarchy on 28 May 2008; the new Constitution came on 20 September 2015.

s: To which party did Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda', the first Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal, belong?
x: Prachanda of the UCPN (Maoist) became the first PM of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal.

s: What is the estimated hydropower potential of Nepal?
x: Nepal's hydropower potential is put at 83,000 MW; the first trilateral power deal had Nepal supplying Bangladesh through the Indian grid.

s: Under the first trilateral power deal in the region, through which route does Nepal supply electricity to Bangladesh?
x: Nepal supplies power to Bangladesh through the Indian grid, the first trilateral power trade.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Look East and Act East policies?
o: Look East was launched in the early 1990s under P.V. Narasimha Rao
Look East was originally economic, focused on trade, investment and AIFTA with ASEAN
Act East was later extended to political, strategic and cultural fields
Act East was launched in 2014 at a SAARC Summit
x: Act East was launched in 2014 at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar under PM Modi, not at a SAARC Summit.

s: What is the main focus of India's Link West (Think West) policy?
o: Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific Islands
x: Link West, also called Think West, focuses on the Gulf, Iran and Israel.

s: At which forum was India's Act East Policy launched in 2014?
x: Act East was launched at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar (2014), not at a SAARC Summit.

s: Under which Prime Minister was India's Look East Policy (1991-92) launched?
x: Look East was launched under P.V. Narasimha Rao; Act East under Narendra Modi.

s: As what kind of policy was the Act East Policy initially conceived?
x: Act East began as an economic policy and was later extended to political, strategic and cultural fields with an Indo-Pacific orientation.

s: Countering China's influence, access to new markets and instability in West and Central Asia were drivers of which policy of India?
x: Countering China, new markets and instability in West and Central Asia were the drivers of the Look East Policy (1991-92).

s: Which is the fourth C added to the Commerce, Culture and Connectivity framework of the Act East Policy?
x: The 4th C is Capacity building, not Climate action.

s: With which country is the Akhaura-Agartala railway link associated?
x: Akhaura-Agartala is a rail link with Bangladesh, not an ASEAN-linked project like Kaladan and the Trilateral Highway.

s: Under the Act East Policy, which region of India is the gateway to ASEAN?
x: The North-East is India's gateway to ASEAN under Act East.

s: In which year did India and Vietnam raise their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership?
x: Under Act East, India-Vietnam ties became a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2016.

s: Which ASEAN country became India's strategic partner in August 2025?
x: India and the Philippines became strategic partners in August 2025; Malaysia's ties became a CSP in 2024.

s: Where was India's Connect Central Asia policy launched in 2012?
x: Connect Central Asia was launched at Bishkek in 2012; Samarkand hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue (2019).

s: In 2026, what did the USA do with India's sanctions waiver for Chabahar port?
x: In 2026 the USA ended, not extended, India's Chabahar waiver; Chabahar gives India access to Afghanistan, Central Asia and the INSTC bypassing Pakistan.

s: What bilateral trade target was set when India-Uzbekistan ties were raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in August 2026?
x: The August 2026 upgrade set a $5 billion trade target by 2030, along with a uranium-supply framework.

s: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers was hosted by which country and held at which city?
x: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019. Afghanistan was also invited.

s: When and how was the first India-Central Asia Summit held?
x: The first India-Central Asia Summit was held virtually in January 2022.

s: On which water body is Iran's Chabahar port located?
x: Chabahar is on the Gulf of Oman and gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia avoiding Pakistan.

s: Besides the Central Asian states, which country was invited to the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019?
x: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers (Samarkand, 2019) also invited Afghanistan.

s: Besides India, Israel and the USA, which country is a member of the I2U2, called the 'West Asia Quad'?
x: I2U2 is India, Israel, UAE and USA.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's Link West engagement:
1. India's trade with the GCC is over $160 billion.
2. The first I2U2 leaders' summit was held virtually in 2022.
3. I2U2 is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: GCC trade exceeds $160 billion, the first I2U2 summit was virtual (2022) and it is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.

s: Which grouping is India's largest socio-economic partner in West Asia, with trade of over $160 billion?
x: The GCC is India's largest socio-economic partner in the region, with over $160 billion trade and about 10 million Indians.

s: India's Think West doctrine has widened in scope into which grouping?
x: Think West (Gulf, Iran, Israel) has widened into I2U2.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's maritime visions?
o: SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region
SAGAR was announced in Sri Lanka in 2015
MAHASAGAR (2025) stands for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
SHANTI was announced on 13 July 2026 by EAM Jaishankar
x: SAGAR (2015) and MAHASAGAR (2025) were both announced in Mauritius, not Sri Lanka.

s: In which sea area is SHANTI, India's normative framework for shared maritime spaces, to be operationalised first?
x: SHANTI is a normative framework for shared maritime spaces to be operationalised first in the Bay of Bengal.

s: Under the SAGAR doctrine, how does India project itself in the Indian Ocean Region?
o: Junior partner of an external power
x: SAGAR presents India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region, partly in response to China's String of Pearls.

s: In which country was SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) announced in 2015?
x: SAGAR was announced in Mauritius in 2015; MAHASAGAR was also announced in Mauritius (2025).

s: Who launched SHANTI, India's framework for shared maritime spaces, on 13 July 2026?
x: SHANTI was launched by EAM Jaishankar, not the PM.

s: In which year was SAGAR upgraded to MAHASAGAR?
x: MAHASAGAR came in 2025 (Mauritius); SAGAR was 2015 and SHANTI 2026.

s: What is the full form of SAGAR in India's maritime policy?
o: Security and Growth for All in the Region
Strategic Alliance for Growth and Regional Security
Security and Governance in the Asian Region
Shared Advancement for Growth in the Region
x: SAGAR, announced in Mauritius in 2015, stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region.

s: What is the full form of MAHASAGAR, India's upgraded maritime vision of 2025?
o: Maritime Alliance for Harmony and Security Across Global and Asian Regions
Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
Multilateral Holistic Approach to Security and Growth in the Asian Region
Mutual Help and Security Agreement for Growth and Regional Advancement
x: MAHASAGAR, announced in Mauritius in 2025, means Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions.

s: What is the full form of SHANTI, India's framework for shared maritime spaces announced in July 2026?
o: Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity
Security and Harmony Among Nations Through Integration
Shared Harbours and Navigation Through Indian Ocean
Strategic Harmony and Norms for Trade in the Indo-Pacific
x: SHANTI, announced by EAM Jaishankar on 13 July 2026, stands for Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity.

s: Indian coastal surveillance radars have been installed in which of the following group of countries?
o: Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles
Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Mauritius and Seychelles
Sri Lanka, Maldives, Bangladesh and Mauritius
x: The coastal radar chain covers Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles.

s: Where was the Information Fusion Centre-Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) inaugurated in December 2018?
x: IFC-IOR was inaugurated on 22 December 2018 at IMAC, Gurugram, hosted by the Indian Navy.

s: With India and Sri Lanka, which country formed the Colombo Security Conclave as a trilateral in 2011?
x: It began as India, Sri Lanka and Maldives; Mauritius, Bangladesh and Seychelles joined later.

s: Which city hosted the MILAN 2026 naval exercise?
x: MILAN 2026 was held at Visakhapatnam, linking Andhra Pradesh to Act East and SAGAR.

s: Which service hosts the Information Fusion Centre-Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) at Gurugram?
x: The IFC-IOR, inaugurated on 22 December 2018 at IMAC, Gurugram, is hosted by the Indian Navy.

s: The coastal radar chain, IFC-IOR and island projects are flagship initiatives of which doctrine?
x: SAGAR (2015) widened into MAHASAGAR and IPOI; its flagships are the radar chain, IFC-IOR and island projects.

s: Where was the 14th East Asia Summit of November 2019, at which PM Modi proposed the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, held?
x: IPOI was proposed at the 14th EAS in Bangkok; it is an open, non-treaty initiative with seven pillars that builds on SAGAR.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative?
x: The seven IPOI pillars include Maritime Security, Maritime Ecology, Maritime Resources, Capacity Building and Resource Sharing, Disaster Risk Reduction and Management, Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation, and Trade, Connectivity and Maritime Transport. Nuclear Disarmament Verification is not one of them.

s: When did PM Modi set out India's free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific vision at the Shangri-La Dialogue?
x: Prime Minister Modi set out this vision, with ASEAN centrality, in his Shangri-La Dialogue keynote in June 2018.

s: Which body organises the Shangri-La Dialogue, held in Singapore since 2002?
x: The Shangri-La Dialogue is run by the London-based IISS and has been held in Singapore since 2002.

s: How many pillars does the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) have?
x: IPOI has seven pillars, from Maritime Security to Trade Connectivity and Maritime Transport.

s: What did the Gujral Doctrine, one of the roots of Neighbourhood First, emphasise?
x: The Gujral Doctrine emphasised non-reciprocity, non-interference and not allowing a country's territory to be used against a neighbour.

s: The leaders of which grouping were invited to the PM's swearing-in in May 2014, marking the launch of Neighbourhood First?
x: SAARC leaders were invited to the May 2014 swearing-in; BIMSTEC leaders were invited in 2019.

s: In 2019, the leaders of which grouping were invited to the PM's swearing-in, extending Neighbourhood First?
x: SAARC leaders were invited in May 2014; BIMSTEC leaders in 2019.

s: In which country is the Agalega airstrip and jetty project located?
x: Agalega is in Mauritius; Assumption Island is in Seychelles; Uthuru Thila Falhu and Hanimaadhoo are in the Maldives.

s: Which of the following island project-country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Assumption Island is in Seychelles, not Maldives; the other pairs are correct.

s: In which country is the Hanimaadhoo airport project located?
x: Hanimaadhoo airport, like the Uthuru Thila Falhu harbour, is in the Maldives.

s: In which country is Assumption Island, linked with an Indian project, located?
x: Assumption Island is in Seychelles; Agalega is in Mauritius.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Vajra Prahar involves Special Forces; Yudh Abhyas is Army, Cope India is Air Force and Tiger Triumph is tri-service amphibious.

s:
Consider the following statements about India–US military exercises:
1. Yudh Abhyas is a naval exercise.
2. Tiger Triumph is a tri-service amphibious exercise.
3. Red Flag is a US Air Force multinational exercise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Tiger Triumph is tri-service and amphibious and Red Flag is a US Air Force multinational exercise; Yudh Abhyas is an Army exercise, so statement 1 is wrong.

s: Cope India is an India-US exercise of which service?
x: Cope India is the Air Force exercise; Malabar is naval and Yudh Abhyas is Army.

s: Vajra Prahar between India and the US is an exercise of which force?
x: Vajra Prahar is a Special Forces exercise; Yudh Abhyas is the Army exercise.

s: Malabar is a naval exercise of India and the USA held along with which other countries?
x: Malabar is a naval exercise of India and the USA with Japan and Australia.

s: In which State was the India-US army exercise Yudh Abhyas held in November 2022?
x: Yudh Abhyas of November 2022 was held in Uttarakhand.

s: In which year was LEMOA, an India-US foundational defence agreement, signed?
x: GSOMIA was signed in 2002, LEMOA in 2016, COMCASA in 2018 and BECA in 2020.

s: What does the STA-1 status, granted by the US to India in 2018, give India?
o: Licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology
Access only to civilian nuclear technology
A veto over US defence exports to third countries
x: STA-1 allows faster, licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology, comparable to NATO allies, without NATO membership.

s:
Consider the following statements about India–US foundational agreements:
1. GSOMIA concerns the protection of shared military information.
2. BECA concerns encrypted communications data and equipment.
3. COMCASA concerns encrypted communications data and equipment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: GSOMIA protects shared military information and COMCASA covers encrypted communications; BECA (2020) concerns geospatial data, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: In which year did the United States designate India as a 'Major Defense Partner'?
x: The United States designated India as a Major Defense Partner in 2016.

s: What does BECA (2020), an India-US foundational agreement, deal with?
o: Geospatial data for navigation and missile targeting
x: BECA covers geospatial (satellite) data; encrypted communications is COMCASA, refuelling is LEMOA and military information is GSOMIA.

s: Which India–US foundational agreement was the first to be signed, in 2002?
x: The order is GSOMIA 2002, LEMOA 2016, COMCASA 2018 and BECA 2020.

s: Which pair of India-US defence milestones both date from 2018?
x: COMCASA and STA-1 status both came in 2018; LEMOA and Major Defense Partner are 2016.

s: Who signed the 10-year India-US defence framework of October 2025 on behalf of India?
x: The 10-year defence framework of October 2025 was signed by US Defence Secretary Hegseth and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh.

s: Which development is regarded as the turning point in India-US relations?
x: The 2008 India-US civil nuclear deal is regarded as the turning point in the relationship.

s: The 'Pivot to Asia' or 'Rebalance' policy of the United States, associated with the Obama era, was announced in which year?
x: The Pivot to Asia, also called the Rebalance, was announced in 2011 during the Obama era to shift greater US strategic attention towards the Asia-Pacific region.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Pressler Amendment?
o: It barred US aid to India over its nuclear programme
It required the US President to certify that Pakistan had no nuclear device
x: The Pressler Amendment barred US aid to Pakistan, not India, unless the President certified Pakistan had no nuclear device; it was applied in 1990.

s: CAATSA (2017) of the USA mainly imposes sanctions on countries that do which of the following?
x: CAATSA provides for US sanctions against buyers of Russian arms; India sought a waiver over its S-400 purchase.

s: How are India-US relations officially described?
x: India-US ties are described as a Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.

s: India sought a CAATSA waiver from the US over its purchase of which Russian system?
x: CAATSA (2017) sanctions buyers of Russian arms; India sought a waiver over the S-400.

s: Indians receive about what share of approved US H-1B visas?
x: Indians get about 71% of approved H-1Bs; a $100,000 fee on new petitions applied from 21 September 2025.

s: From 21 September 2025, what fee did the USA impose on new H-1B visa petitions?
x: The US set a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions from 21 September 2025.

s: Which country has the world's largest Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) community?
x: The United States has the largest PIO community; Malaysia is second.

s: According to the RBI survey (2023-24), what share of India's remittances comes from the US?
x: The US is India's largest source of remittances at 27.7%, ahead of the UAE.

s: Which language was the fastest-growing foreign language in the US during 2010-17?
x: Telugu was the fastest-growing foreign language in the US between 2010 and 2017.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian diaspora in the USA:
1. The 2020 Census counted about 4.4 million 'Indian-alone' people, the largest Asian-alone group.
2. The UAE sends India more remittances than the US.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the US is the largest source (27.7%), ahead of the UAE.

s: Who was the first Indian American elected to the US Congress, in 1956?
x: Dalip Singh Saund won a House seat from California in 1956, the first Indian American (and first Asian American) in Congress.

s: Kovvada, the proposed site for Westinghouse AP1000 reactors, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kovvada is in Srikakulam district and is the proposed site for the Westinghouse AP1000 reactors under India-US nuclear cooperation.

s: In which year was the Hyde Act, which made the India-US civil nuclear deal possible under US law, passed?
x: The Hyde Act of 2006 came before the 123 Agreement of 2008.

s: When did the NSG grant India the clean waiver that allowed civil nuclear trade?
x: The Nuclear Suppliers Group gave India a clean waiver in September 2008.

s:
Arrange the steps of the India-US civil nuclear deal in chronological order:
1. 123 Agreement
2. Hyde Act
3. NSG clean waiver
x: Hyde Act (2006), then the 123 Agreement (2008), then the NSG clean waiver (September 2008).

s: Which agreement of 2008 is the India-US civil nuclear cooperation agreement?
x: The 123 Agreement of 2008 is the civil nuclear cooperation agreement; the Hyde Act of 2006 is the US law that made it possible.

s: Which reactors are proposed at Kovvada in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh under India-US civil nuclear cooperation?
x: Kovvada (Srikakulam) is the proposed site for Westinghouse AP1000 reactors.

s: With which company are GE F414 jet engines to be co-produced in India?
x: GE F414 engines are to be co-produced with HAL, not BEL; iCET (2023) was relaunched as TRUST in 2025.

s: What is the outlay of the India Semiconductor Mission launched in December 2021?
x: The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in December 2021 with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.

s: India became which signatory of the Artemis Accords in June 2023?
x: India signed the Artemis Accords in June 2023 as the 27th signatory.

s: Under what name was the India-US Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology (iCET) relaunched in 2025?
x: iCET (2023) was relaunched as TRUST in February 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India-US technology cooperation?
o: GE F414 jet engines are to be co-produced with BEL
TRUST added critical minerals such as lithium and rare earths
TRUST added biotechnology to semiconductors, AI and quantum
x: GE F414 engines are to be co-produced with HAL, not BEL.

s: When did the United States withdraw India's Generalized System of Preferences (GSP) benefits?
x: The United States withdrew India's GSP benefits in June 2019.

s: By which year does Mission 500, announced in the February 2025 Modi-Trump joint statement, aim to take India-US trade to $500 billion?
x: Mission 500, from the February 2025 Modi-Trump joint statement, aims to take India-US bilateral trade to $500 billion by 2030.

s: From 27 August 2025, what was the total US duty on Indian goods?
x: An extra 25% over Russian oil purchases took the total US duty on Indian goods to 50%.

s: In which year did the India-US Strategic and Commercial Dialogue begin?
x: The Strategic and Commercial Dialogue dates from 2015; the 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue from 2018.

s: In which year was the first India-US 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue held?
x: The 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue began in 2018; the Strategic and Commercial Dialogue dates from 2015.

s: In which year was the first leaders' summit of the Quad (India, US, Japan, Australia) held?
x: The first Quad leaders' summit was held in 2021.

s: With which African country did India establish a strategic partnership in 2023?
x: India and Tanzania became strategic partners in 2023, the year IIT Madras Zanzibar opened.

s: In which year was IIT Madras Zanzibar in Tanzania established?
x: IIT Madras Zanzibar was established in 2023, the year Tanzania became India's strategic partner.

s: Where was the II India-Africa Forum Summit (2011) held?
x: The I (2008) and III (2015) Summits were in New Delhi; the II Summit (2011) was in Addis Ababa.

s: Under which country's G20 presidency did the African Union become a permanent member of the G20 in 2023?
x: The African Union joined the G20 as a permanent member in 2023 during India's presidency.

s: Where was the III India-Africa Forum Summit (2015), attended by all 54 African states, held?
x: IAFS-I (2008) and IAFS-III (2015) were in New Delhi; IAFS-II (2011) was in Addis Ababa.

s: Where was the first Mahatma Gandhi Convention Centre in Africa opened in January 2020?
x: India's first Mahatma Gandhi Convention Centre in Africa opened at Niamey, Niger, in January 2020.

s: What is India's e-VBAB (e-VidyaBharati and e-ArogyaBharati) network for Africa meant for?
x: e-VidyaBharati gives tele-education and e-ArogyaBharati gives tele-medicine to African countries.

s: In which African country did India open a new High Commission in October 2019?
x: India opened a new High Commission in Sierra Leone in October 2019.

s: Where was the first India-Africa Forum Summit held in 2008?
x: IAFS-I (2008) and IAFS-III (2015) were in New Delhi; IAFS-II (2011) was in Addis Ababa.

s: What kind of partnership do India and Japan share?
x: India and Japan have a Special Strategic and Global Partnership.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India-Japan economic ties?
o: Japan is India's largest source of FDI
At the 15th Annual Summit (2025), Japanese firms committed 10 trillion yen over ten years
The 10 trillion yen commitment is worth about $67 billion
x: Japan is India's 5th-largest FDI source, not the largest; the CEPA (2011) and the 10 trillion yen (~$67 billion) commitment are correct.

s: The Mumbai–Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project, supported by Japanese ODA, uses which technology?
x: The project uses Japan's Shinkansen technology with Japanese ODA support.

s: In which year did India and Japan sign the Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement (ACSA)?
x: The India-Japan ACSA was signed in 2020; 2011 is the CEPA.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India–UAE relations?
o: They have had a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership since 2017
The India-UAE CEPA became operational in 2022
The UAE is India's second-largest trading partner
Bilateral trade exceeded $100 billion in FY 2024-25
x: With over $100 billion in trade, the UAE is India's third-largest trading partner, not second.

s: When did the India-Oman CEPA, signed in December 2025, enter into force?
x: The CEPA entered into force on 1 June 2026, with Oman giving 99% duty-free access to Indian exports.

s: The UAE was India's first foreign investor in which of the following?
o: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project
The Strategic Petroleum Reserve at Mangaluru
x: The UAE became the first foreign investor in India's Strategic Petroleum Reserve at Mangaluru.

s: When was the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) launched at the G20 New Delhi summit?
x: IMEC, with an eastern and a northern corridor, was launched at the G20 New Delhi summit in September 2023.

s: The India-Oman CEPA is India's ____ CEPA with a GCC country.
x: Oman is India's second GCC CEPA, after the UAE.

s: In which year did India and Saudi Arabia set up a Strategic Partnership Council?
x: The India-Saudi Strategic Partnership Council dates from 2019; 2017 is the UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

s: According to the RBI survey for 2023-24, which country is India's second-largest source of remittances?
x: The UAE sent 19.2% of India's remittances in 2023-24, second only to the US (27.7%).

s: Full diplomatic relations between India and Israel were established in which year under which Indian Prime Minister?
x: India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992 during the P. V. Narasimha Rao government.

s: Where is the Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for vegetables and flowers in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The AP Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for vegetables and flowers is at Kuppam.

s: The I2U2 grouping brings together India, Israel, the USA and which other country?
x: I2U2 = India, Israel, UAE and USA.

s: In which year did Narendra Modi become the first Indian Prime Minister to visit Israel?
x: Narendra Modi visited Israel in 2017, the first visit by an Indian Prime Minister.

s: Under the Abraham Accords of 2020, Israel normalised ties with which of the following Arab countries?
x: Under the Abraham Accords, Israel normalised ties with four Arab countries, including Bahrain and the UAE, in 2020.

s: Defence, including joint research and development, is a key pillar of which partnership of India with Israel?
x: India and Israel have a Special Strategic Partnership, with defence, including joint R&D, as a key pillar.

s: In which year was the Declaration on Strategic Partnership between India and Russia signed?
x: India and Russia signed the Declaration on Strategic Partnership in 2000, later developing it into a Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 23rd India–Russia Annual Summit (New Delhi)?
o: It marked the 25th anniversary of the strategic partnership
It set a $100 billion trade target by 2030
About 96% of bilateral trade is settled in national currencies
x: Russia joined the International Big Cat Alliance; I2U2 is India, Israel, UAE and USA.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The India-Russia S-400 deal dates to 2018. BrahMos is an India-Russia venture, Kudankulam is in Tamil Nadu and Kovvada is in Andhra Pradesh.

s: In which State is the Kudankulam nuclear power plant, built with Russian cooperation, located?
x: Kudankulam is in Tamil Nadu; Kovvada is the proposed site in Andhra Pradesh.

s: In which year did India sign the S-400 air defence deal with Russia?
x: The S-400 deal with Russia was signed in 2018.

s: About what share of India-Russia trade is settled in national currencies?
x: About 96% of India-Russia trade is in national currencies (rupee-rouble).

s: Through which port does the International North-South Transport Corridor, connecting India, Iran and Russia, run?
x: The INSTC's main route runs from Mumbai by sea to Bandar Abbas in Iran and then overland through Iran and the Caspian region to Russia. Chabahar is being linked to it; Gwadar is in Pakistan and Jebel Ali in the UAE.

s: The name 'BrahMos' is taken from which two rivers?
x: BrahMos is an India-Russia joint venture named after the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.

s: With which country's help were the Bhilai and Bokaro steel plants built?
x: Bhilai and Bokaro were built with Soviet help and are anchors of India-Russia ties.

s: In which year did India sign the Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation with the Soviet Union?
x: The Indo-Soviet Treaty of 1971 is an anchor of India-Russia relations.

s: Which alliance did Russia join at the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit in New Delhi?
x: At the 23rd Annual Summit, Russia joined the India-led International Big Cat Alliance.

s: With the FTA concluded at the 16th India-EU Summit (2026), the EU became India's ____ FTA partner.
x: The FTA concluded at the 16th Summit made the EU India's 22nd FTA partner; a Security and Defence Partnership was also signed.

s: When did India and the UK sign the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)?
x: The India-UK CETA was signed in July 2025.

s: What is the full form of BTIA in the context of India-European Union relations?
x: BTIA stands for India-EU Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement; negotiations have been underway since 2007.

s: In which year was the India-EU Trade and Technology Council set up?
x: The Trade and Technology Council dates from 2022; BTIA talks began in 2007 and the first Strategic Dialogue was in 2025.

s: With which country did India sign its first comprehensive FTA, the CECA of 2005?
x: The CECA with Singapore (2005) was India's first comprehensive FTA.

s: When did the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) enter into force?
x: TEPA was signed in March 2024 and entered into force on 1 October 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's trade agreements:
1. The CECPA with Mauritius dates from 2021.
2. The ECTA with Australia dates from 2022.
3. The CEPA with the UAE dates from 2011.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: CECPA (Mauritius) is 2021 and ECTA (Australia) 2022; the UAE CEPA is 2022 (2011 is Japan's CEPA), so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Indra is a tri-service military exercise between India and which country?
x: Indra is the India-Russia tri-service exercise, first held in 2017.

s: With which countries does India hold the air force exercise Desert Knight?
x: Desert Knight is an Air Force exercise with France and the UAE.

s: Which of the following exercise–partner pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Garuda is the India-France Air Force exercise, not with Russia.

s: JIMEX is a naval exercise between India and which country?
x: JIMEX is the Japan-India Maritime Exercise of the two navies.

s: Which is the only principal organ of the UN whose decisions are binding on member states?
x: Only the Security Council's decisions bind UN members.

s: In the April 2024 UNSC vote on full UN membership for Palestine, which country used its veto?
x: The United States vetoed the proposal, while the United Kingdom and Switzerland abstained.

s: Which Article of the UN Charter bars the immediate re-election of a retiring non-permanent member of the Security Council?
x: Article 23 bars immediate re-election of a retiring non-permanent member; Article 27 is the veto and Article 18 two-thirds voting in the UNGA.

s: In the April 2024 UNSC vote on full UN membership for Palestine, which two members abstained?
x: The USA vetoed; the UK and Switzerland abstained.

s: Which of the following groups consists only of permanent members of the UN Security Council?
x: The P5 are China, France, Russia, the UK and the USA; Germany, India, Japan and Brazil are not permanent members.

s: For what term are the non-permanent members of the UN Security Council elected?
x: The 10 non-permanent members are elected by the UNGA for two years and cannot be re-elected at once.

s: Which UNSC Resolution created the Counter-Terrorism Committee after 9/11?
x: 1373 (2001) set up the Counter-Terrorism Committee; 1267 covers Al-Qaida/ISIL sanctions and 1540 WMD and non-state actors.

s: Where did India conduct its first capacity-building programme on UNSCR 1540 for Asia-Pacific countries in February 2025?
x: The programme was held at the National Academy of Customs, Indirect Taxes and Narcotics (NACIN), Palasamudram, Andhra Pradesh, in February 2025.

s: What is the aim of UNSC Resolution 1540 (2004)?
o: Stop weapons of mass destruction reaching non-state actors
Let the UNGA act when a veto blocks the UNSC
x: Resolution 1540 targets WMD reaching non-state actors; 1267 is Al-Qaida/ISIL sanctions and 1373 the Counter-Terrorism Committee.

s: The Charter of the United Nations was signed by 50 nations at which place and on which date?
x: The UN Charter was signed by 50 nations at San Francisco on 26 June 1945.

s: What is required to amend the UN Charter, for example for UNSC reform?
o: A simple majority of members, including all five permanent members
A two-thirds majority of members, including ratification by all five permanent members
A two-thirds majority of members, without needing the permanent members
Unanimous approval of all UN members
x: A Charter amendment needs a two-thirds majority of members and ratification by all five permanent members of the Security Council.

s: Which of the following is NOT a purpose listed in Article 1 of the UN Charter?
x: Sovereign equality is stated in Article 2, not Article 1.

s: Which are the working languages of the UN?
x: Of the six official languages, English and French are the working languages.

s: Sovereign equality of members is laid down in which Article of the UN Charter?
x: Article 2 lays down sovereign equality; Article 1 lists the purposes.

s: On which date did the Charter of the United Nations come into force?
x: The Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, observed as UN Day. 26 June 1945 is when 50 nations signed it at San Francisco. 1 January 1942 and 10 January 1946 are not the dates given for the Charter's entry into force.

s: How many member states does the United Nations have?
x: The United Nations has 193 member states.

s: Which Article of the UN Charter gives the veto power to the five permanent members?
x: Article 27 provides the veto of the P5; Article 18 deals with two-thirds votes in the UNGA and Article 23 bars immediate re-election.

s: Under which Article of the UN Charter do 'important questions' in the General Assembly need a two-thirds majority?
x: Article 18 says important questions in the UNGA need a two-thirds majority.

s: Which country ratified the UN Charter on 16 October 1945 to become the 51st original member?
x: Poland was absent at San Francisco and ratified the Charter on 16 October 1945 as the 51st original member.

s: When did the ICJ give its unanimous advisory opinion on climate obligations?
x: The ICJ issued the unanimous climate advisory opinion in July 2025.

s: Which of the following pairs about the International Court of Justice is correctly matched?
o: Electing body – UN General Assembly alone
x: The ICJ has 15 judges with 9-year terms, elected by the UNGA and the UNSC voting separately.

s: Which Indian judge served as President of the International Court of Justice during 1985–1988?
x: Nagendra Singh, one of the Indian judges of the ICJ, served as its President from 1985 to 1988.

s: In the Kulbhushan Jadhav case (2019), which convention did the ICJ hold that Pakistan had breached?
x: The ICJ held that Pakistan breached the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations and ordered a review of Jadhav's conviction.

s: The UN Trusteeship Council has been inactive since 1994, after which trust territory attained self-government?
x: Palau, the last trust territory, became self-governing in 1994, after which the Trusteeship Council became inactive.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: International Court of Justice — Principal judicial organ — The Hague
x: ECOSOC has 54 members serving three-year terms, not 15 members serving two-year terms. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which commission reviewed Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration before being replaced by the High-Level Political Forum in 2013?
o: Commission on the Status of Women
x: The Commission on Sustainable Development reviewed Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration and was replaced by the High-Level Political Forum in 2013.

s: How many members does the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) have, and for what term?
x: ECOSOC has 54 members with 3-year terms.

s: In which year was the Commission on the Status of Women, a functional commission of ECOSOC, set up?
x: The Commission on the Status of Women dates from 1946.

s: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt the 'Uniting for Peace' resolution (Resolution 377)?
x: Resolution 377 was adopted in 1950 and first used in the 1956 Suez Crisis.

s: How many members does the UNGA Credentials Committee have, appointed each session?
x: The Credentials Committee has 9 members appointed each session.

s: During which of the following was the 'Uniting for Peace' resolution first used to send peacekeepers?
x: Adopted in 1950, Uniting for Peace was first used in the 1956 Suez Crisis.

s: Which are the two non-member observer States at the United Nations?
o: Holy See and State of Palestine
x: The Holy See (since 1964) and the State of Palestine (2012, res. 67/19) are the two non-member observer States.

s: Who is the President of the 81st UN General Assembly (2026-27)?
x: Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh, who defeated Cyprus's candidate, presides over the 81st UNGA.

s: Who among the following Indians served as President of the UN General Assembly?
x: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit served as President of the UN General Assembly (1953), the first woman to hold the post.

s: Who was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations?
x: Trygve Lie took office in 1946, followed by Hammarskjold (1953), U Thant (1961) and Waldheim (1972).

s: Who was the first African Secretary-General of the United Nations?
x: Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt was the first African SG; Kofi Annan came after him. U Thant was the first Asian SG.

s: Who was the first Asian Secretary-General of the United Nations?
x: U Thant of Burma (1961-71) was the first Asian Secretary-General.

s: Kofi Annan, the second African Secretary-General of the UN, belonged to which country?
x: Kofi Annan was from Ghana; Boutros Boutros-Ghali (Egypt) was the first African SG.

s: To which country does the present UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres belong?
x: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General since 2017, is from Portugal.

s: Who was the first Latin American Secretary-General of the United Nations?
x: Javier Perez de Cuellar of Peru (1982-91) was the first Latin American Secretary-General.

s: Dag Hammarskjold, the second Secretary-General of the UN, belonged to which country?
x: Dag Hammarskjold (1953-61) was from Sweden; Trygve Lie, the first, was from Norway.

s: How many times had India served as an elected non-permanent member of the UN Security Council through the 2021–22 term?
Who was the first woman to serve as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York?
x: Ruchira Kamboj was the first woman Permanent Representative of India to the UN (BPSC 2024). Sushma Swaraj was External Affairs Minister, not PR. Nirupama Rao was Foreign Secretary. Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was President of the UN General Assembly, not India's PR in New York.

s: What is the number of the UNGA resolution of 11 December 2014 that proclaimed 21 June as International Day of Yoga?
x: Resolution 69/131 was adopted by consensus with 177 co-sponsors.

s: As what did India, a founding member of the UN, sign the Charter in June 1945?
x: India signed the Charter as British India in June 1945.

s: Who was the first to address the UN General Assembly in Hindi, in 1977?
x: Atal Bihari Vajpayee, as External Affairs Minister, gave the first Hindi speech at the UNGA on 4 October 1977.

s: In which year did Atal Bihari Vajpayee deliver the first Hindi speech at the UN General Assembly?
x: Vajpayee spoke in Hindi at the UNGA on 4 October 1977, as External Affairs Minister.

s: India's bid for a non-permanent seat of the UN Security Council launched in July 2026 is for which term?
x: EAM Jaishankar launched India's bid for the 2028-29 UNSC term in New York on 13 July 2026.

s: The UNGA resolution of 2014 that proclaimed 21 June as International Day of Yoga had how many co-sponsors?
x: Resolution 69/131 was adopted by consensus with 177 co-sponsors.

s: Who has been India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York since September 2024?
x: Parvathaneni Harish succeeded Ruchira Kamboj as India's PR in September 2024.

s: What does the Ezulwini Consensus (2005) demand for Africa?
o: Two permanent seats with veto, plus five non-permanent seats
x: Ezulwini demands two permanent seats with veto plus five non-permanent seats for Africa.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: G4 — Opposition to permanent seats for Africa
Uniting for Consensus — Demand for new permanent seats
L.69 — Developing countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific
Ezulwini Consensus — Abolition of all non-permanent seats
x: The L.69 group consists of developing countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific. The G4 supports permanent seats, Uniting for Consensus opposes new permanent seats, and Ezulwini seeks African representation.

s: The Inter-Governmental Negotiations (IGN) on UNSC reform are an informal process of which UN organ?
x: The IGN is an informal working process of the UN General Assembly, not a Security Council body.

s: Which country leads the Uniting for Consensus ('Coffee Club') group on UNSC reform?
x: Uniting for Consensus is led by Italy and includes Pakistan.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about groups on UNSC reform?
o: The G4 comprises Brazil, Germany, India and Japan
India is a member of the L.69 group
Uniting for Consensus supports new permanent seats
Pakistan is part of Uniting for Consensus
x: Uniting for Consensus opposes new permanent seats.

s: In which year were the Inter-Governmental Negotiations (IGN) on UNSC reform set up?
x: The IGN, an informal UNGA process on UNSC reform, was set up in 2008.

s: UN specialised agencies, autonomous bodies with their own treaties and budgets, are linked to which UN organ?
x: Specialised agencies are autonomous, with their own treaties and budgets, and are linked to ECOSOC; creation by the General Assembly with voluntary funding describes funds and programmes.

s: How is the UNHCR, set up in 1950 for refugee protection, classified in the UN system?
o: An Office of the General Assembly
A specialised agency linked to ECOSOC
A related organisation reporting to the UNSC
A financial institution of the World Bank Group
x: UNHCR (1950, Geneva) is an Office of the General Assembly for refugee protection, not a specialised agency.

s: Which of the following is a specialised agency of the United Nations?
x: IFAD is a UN specialised agency as well as an international financial institution serving rural poor populations.

s: Which UN body has the mandate to protect refugees?
x: Refugees are UNHCR's mandate; UNICEF deals with children's rights and UNEP with climate, biodiversity and pollution.

s: Which UN body is both a specialised agency and an international financial institution for the rural poor?
x: IFAD is both a specialised agency and an international financial institution; WFP, UNDP and UNICEF are funds and programmes.

s: Besides UNEP, which UN body is headquartered at Nairobi?
x: Nairobi hosts UNEP and UN-Habitat; IFAD and WFP are in Rome.

s: Which of the following is a related organisation and NOT a specialised agency of the UN?
x: The IAEA, like the WTO and OPCW, is a related organisation, not a specialised agency.

s: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), set up after the 1972 Stockholm Conference?
x: UNEP was created in 1972 following the Stockholm Conference and has its HQ at Nairobi, Kenya. Geneva hosts WHO/ILO/ITU, Vienna hosts UNIDO/IAEA, and New York hosts UNICEF.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The WHO is headquartered at Geneva and was founded in 1948.
2. The FAO was founded on 16 October 1945 and is headquartered at Rome.
3. The World Food Programme was founded in 1961 and is headquartered at Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: WHO, Geneva, 1948 (7 April). Statement 2 is correct: FAO, Rome, 16 October 1945. Statement 3 is wrong: WFP was founded in 1961 but its HQ is Rome, not Geneva. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, while C and D wrongly include statement 3.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: IFAD is headquartered in Rome and was founded in 1977. WFP is headquartered in Rome, UPU in Bern and UNIDO in Vienna.

s: Where is the headquarters of UNICEF, founded in 1946?
x: UNICEF was founded in 1946 and its headquarters is in New York, not Geneva.

s:
Consider the following statements about the International Labour Organization:
1. It was founded in 1919.
2. It became a UN specialised agency in 1946.
3. It is headquartered at Rome.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: ILO was founded in 1919. Statement 2 is correct: it became a UN specialised agency in 1946. Statement 3 is wrong: ILO is headquartered at Geneva; Rome hosts FAO, IFAD and WFP. So 1 and 2 only.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Universal Postal Union (UPU), founded in 1874?
x: The UPU (1874) is headquartered at Bern.

s: Which of the following UN bodies is headquartered at Rome?
x: WFP is in Rome (with FAO and IFAD); the ILO, WHO and ITU are in Geneva.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)?
x: ICAO (1947) is headquartered at Montreal; London hosts the IMO.

s: Which of the following UN specialised agencies is the oldest, founded in 1865?
x: The ITU dates from 1865 (International Telegraph Union); the UPU from 1874, the ILO from 1919 and WIPO from 1967.

s: Which of the following pairs of agency and founding year is correctly matched?
x: IFAD was founded in 1977. WIPO dates from 1967, IMO from 1948 and WFP from 1961.

s: In which year was UNICEF established?
x: UNICEF was set up in 1946 and has its headquarters at New York.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Maritime Organization (IMO)?
x: The IMO, founded in 1948, is headquartered at London.

s: Where is the headquarters of the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)?
x: WIPO, set up in 1967, is headquartered at Geneva.

s: Where is the headquarters of UNESCO, of which India is a founding member?
x: UNESCO (1945) is headquartered at Paris; India is a founding member.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Body)
A. IAEA
B. ICAO
C. UPU
D. IMO
List-II (Headquarters)
1. Bern
2. Vienna
3. London
4. Montreal
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: IAEA is at Vienna, ICAO at Montreal, UPU at Bern and IMO at London.

s: The Information for All Programme is associated with which organisation?
x: The Information for All Programme, or IFAP, is a UNESCO programme.

s: How many member states did UNESCO have in 2025-26?
x: UNESCO has 194 members and 12 associate members, with a 58-member Executive Board.

s: Who became Director-General of UNESCO on 15 November 2025, the first Arab to hold the post?
x: Khaled El-Enany of Egypt became UNESCO DG on 15 November 2025, the first Arab DG.

s:
Consider the following statements about UNESCO:
1. It runs the Man and the Biosphere Programme.
2. It leads SDG-4 on Education 2030.
3. It compiles the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: UNESCO runs the Man and the Biosphere Programme and leads SDG-4; the Global MPI is built by UNDP and OPHI.

s: The World Heritage Convention was adopted in which year?
x: The World Heritage Convention was adopted in 1972.

s: Where was the World Heritage Committee session of July 2026 held, at which Sarnath became India's 45th World Heritage Site?
x: Sarnath was inscribed at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea, in July 2026.

s: Which was the first Indian World Heritage site, inscribed along with Ellora?
x: Ajanta, along with Ellora, was India's first World Heritage site inscription in 1983.

s: Which Indian city became India's second UNESCO City of Gastronomy, after Hyderabad (2019)?
x: Lucknow followed Hyderabad as India's second City of Gastronomy.

s: In which year were the Hoysala temples of Karnataka inscribed on the World Heritage List?
x: The Hoysala temples were inscribed in September 2023.

s: In which year was Yoga inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
x: Yoga was inscribed on the Intangible Heritage list in 2016. 2019 is the year of Hyderabad's gastronomy designation and 2025 (December) is Deepavali's inscription; 2014 is not the year of any of these inscriptions.

s: Which of the following was placed on India's Tentative List for World Heritage in 2022?
x: Lepakshi in Andhra Pradesh was placed on India's Tentative List in 2022; the others are inscribed World Heritage sites.

s: On which UNESCO list are the Bhagavad Gita manuscripts and the Natyashastra inscribed?
x: The Bhagavad Gita manuscripts and the Natyashastra are on the Memory of the World register.

s: Where was the Committee session of December 2025 held, at which Deepavali was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list?
x: Deepavali was inscribed at the 20th Intergovernmental Committee at the Red Fort in December 2025.

s: Which is the nodal body in India for UNESCO World Heritage properties?
o: Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage
x: The ASI is the nodal body and looks after 28 World Heritage properties.

s: Which Indian property was inscribed on the World Heritage List at the 47th session in Paris in 2025?
x: Maratha Military Landscapes were inscribed at the 47th session, Paris, 2025.

s: The Global Environment Facility, established in 1992, is run in partnership by which of the following?
x: The GEF is a financial mechanism operated in partnership by UNDP, UNEP and the World Bank.

s: The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) is jointly associated with which group?
o: FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO
UNDP, UNEP, UNESCO, ILO and UNHCR
FAO, UNFPA, WIPO, WTO and IAEA
WHO, UNESCO, ICAO, IMO and ITU
x: SOFI is jointly published by FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO.

s: Which UN body builds the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index jointly with OPHI?
x: UNDP co-builds the Global MPI with OPHI (2010).

s: Which UN body deals with population issues and publishes the State of World Population report?
x: UNFPA deals with population and publishes the State of World Population.

s: India signed a five-year rice supply agreement in 2026 with which organisation?
x: India signed a five-year rice supply agreement with the World Food Programme in 2026.

s: With which Indian ministry did the WHO sign the March 2022 agreement for the Global Centre for Traditional Medicine at Jamnagar?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: The WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine at Jamnagar was set up under an agreement with the Ministry of AYUSH in March 2022.

s: Which pair of ILO Fundamental Conventions has India not ratified?
x: India has not ratified C87 (Freedom of Association) and C98 (Right to Organise and Collective Bargaining); the other pairs are ratified.

s: According to the ILO-UNICEF joint estimate for 2020 (released 2021), about how many child labourers were there in the world?
x: The ILO–UNICEF joint estimate places the number of child labourers globally at 160 million.

s: Besides the International Labour Conference, in which body does the ILO's tripartite structure operate?
x: The ILO's tripartite bodies are the International Labour Conference and the Governing Body, not ECOSOC.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding India and ILO conventions:
1. India has ratified C29 and C105.
2. India has ratified C100 and C111.
3. India has ratified C189 on Domestic Workers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: India has ratified C29, C105, C100 and C111. It has not ratified the Domestic Workers Convention C189, adopted by the ILC in 2011.

s: In which year was the ILO Domestic Workers Convention (C189), which India has not ratified, adopted?
x: C189 on domestic workers was adopted in 2011 and India has not ratified it.

s: In which year did India ratify the ILO conventions on Minimum Age (C138) and Worst Forms of Child Labour (C182)?
x: India ratified C138 and C182 in 2017.

s: According to the ILO-UNICEF estimate released in 2025, about how many child labourers were there in 2024?
x: Child labour fell from 160 million (2020) to about 138 million (2024, released 2025).

s: Which report is published by UNFPA?
x: The State of World Population is a flagship report of UNFPA.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: World Employment and Social Outlook — UNESCO
x: The Human Development Report is a flagship UNDP publication. The other reports are associated respectively with UNFPA, UNEP and ILO.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a UNESCO report?
x: The Emissions Gap Report is published by UNEP. The other three reports are associated with UNESCO.

s: According to the Emissions Gap Report 2025, about how much warming do current policies put the world on course for?
x: The report projects about 2.8°C under current policies and 2.3-2.5°C if NDCs are fully implemented.

s: Which organisation publishes the World Employment and Social Outlook?
x: The World Employment and Social Outlook is an ILO report.

s: According to SOFI 2026, to about what level did global hunger fall for the third year?
x: SOFI 2026 reported hunger falling for the third year to 7.8% (645 million).

s: Which organisation publishes the Human Development Report?
x: UNDP publishes the Human Development Report and builds the Global MPI with OPHI.

s: According to the ILO's Employment and Social Trends 2026, what is the global unemployment rate?
x: ILO Trends 2026 put global unemployment at 4.9% (186 million).

s: The Nobel Peace Prize awarded to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) was received in which years?
x: UNHCR received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and again in 1981.

s: In which year did UNICEF win the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: UNICEF won in 1965, the ILO in 1969, UN Peacekeeping Forces in 1988, and the UN with Kofi Annan in 2001.

s: In which year did the International Labour Organization win the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: The ILO won in 1969; UNICEF in 1965, UNHCR in 1954 and UN Peacekeeping Forces in 1988.

s: Which of the following pairs of Nobel Peace Prize winner and year is correctly matched?
x: UN Peacekeeping Forces won in 1988. The UN with Kofi Annan won in 2001, IPCC with Al Gore in 2007 and UNICEF in 1965.

s: In which year did the World Food Programme (WFP) receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: WFP received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020, not 2019; OPCW won in 2013 and IPCC with Al Gore in 2007.

s: In which year did the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) win the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: The OPCW won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: International Day of Yoga is associated with the UN General Assembly, not UNHCR.

s: Which one of the following pairs of International Day and date is correctly matched?
x: World Food Day (FAO) is on 16 October, the FAO's founding date. World Refugee Day (UNHCR) is 20 June, World Health Day (WHO) is 7 April and the International Day of Yoga is 21 June, so the other pairs are mismatched.

s: World Food Day, 16 October, marks the founding date of which organisation?
x: World Food Day (16 October) is the FAO's founding date.

s: On which date is World Refugee Day, linked to the UNHCR, observed?
x: World Refugee Day is 20 June; 5 June is World Environment Day, 21 June Yoga Day and 7 April World Health Day.

s: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, serving a second term to August 2027, is the Director-General of which organisation?
x: Tedros is WHO Director-General, his second term running to 15 August 2027.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's roles in UN bodies:
1. Dr Harsh Vardhan chaired the WHO Executive Board in 2020-21.
2. Apurva Chandra chaired the ILO Governing Body in 2020-21.
3. India chaired UNODC in March 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India chaired the 68th session of the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, not UNODC.

s: India chaired the 68th session of which UN body in March 2025?
o: UN Office on Drugs and Crime
x: India chaired the 68th session of the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, an ECOSOC functional commission; UNODC is the secretariat.

s: Who is the Director-General of the International Labour Organization?
x: Gilbert F. Houngbo heads the ILO (May 2026).

s: For which term was India re-elected to the Council of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)?
x: India was re-elected to the ICAO Council for 2025-2028.
